citations.quote: The CDKN2A homozygous deletion may qualify the patient for investigational CDK4/6 inhibitor studies

candidates.description: Loss of both alleles of the CDKN2A tumor suppressor gene, identified via next-generation sequencing (NGS).
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the 'Genomic Findings' table in the NGS report and check the 'Alteration' column for 'CDKN2A' and the phrase 'Homozygous deletion'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if the NGS report specifies a 'homozygous deletion' of CDKN2A; negative if the gene is reported as wild-type or no deletion is noted. Absence of mention is not a negative measurement.
candidates.name: CDKN2A homozygous deletion
candidates.uncertainty: The exact genomic region affected (e.g., specific exons 1-3) may vary between patients.

candidates.description: Presence of the specific activating missense mutation p.G12C (c.34G>T) in the KRAS gene.
candidates.extraction_instruction: In the NGS 'Genomic Findings' section, locate 'KRAS' in the Gene column and verify if the 'Alteration' or 'Protein Change' is 'G12C' or 'c.34G>T'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if the NGS report explicitly lists the KRAS p.G12C or c.34G>T mutation; negative if KRAS is reported as wild-type or a different KRAS mutation is identified. Absence of mention is not a negative measurement.
candidates.name: KRAS G12C mutation
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the variant allele frequency (VAF) significantly modifies the clinical role beyond the binary presence of the mutation.

limitations: Small number of patients provided in the evidence snippets.
Lack of consistency in reporting formats across different laboratory reports (e.g., different table structures).
summary: The provided evidence contains genomic profiling results from multiple patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), highlighting recurrent alterations in CDKN2A and KRAS, particularly in squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma histologies.
